target_customer: Households in under-served San Francisco neighborhoods (Portola, Bayview) buying home broadband, and individuals who wanted to start local ISPs
problem: Many homes lacked affordable broadband; Necto offered a starter kit for running a local internet service provider and sold fast home internet itself.
business_model: Residential broadband subscription (flat monthly fee) plus ISP starter kit

founders.name: Adam Montgomery
founders.background_notes: YC bio: trying to make physical infrastructure better with software. Named a founder in the March 2019 acquisition press release.

founders.name: Benjamin Huang
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page; named a founder in the acquisition press release.

exit.reason: Monkeybrains acquired Necto's San Francisco and Oakland operations, terms undisclosed; the founders planned other projects

competitors.name: Starry
competitors.what: Fixed wireless home internet at about 50 dollars a month in Boston, Washington and Los Angeles
competitors.traction_then: launched January 2018 per the search summary; subscriber numbers not stated

competitors.name: Common Networks
competitors.what: Fixed wireless broadband for suburban markets in the western US

technical_complexity.rationale: Building and operating a wireless or fiber last mile network needs radio engineering, rooftop access and billing software, which is standard networking work with physical field operations.

defensibility.rationale: Local installed customers gave some stickiness, but no spectrum, exclusive access or patents are documented.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: The local ISP Monkeybrains bought the operations in March 2019 rather than competing.

market_need_then: The acquisition release says many Necto customers were getting home broadband for the first time, in neighborhoods of San Francisco where options were limited.

branding.domain_note: Used joinnecto.com rather than necto.com (a prefix domain).

identity.voice_and_tone: Site pitches fast internet from your neighborhood provider with clear, affordable pricing

brand_strength.rationale: Brand searches returned unrelated companies named Necto; no coverage of the brand itself was found.

outcome_analysis: Necto went through YC in Winter 2018, raised a small seed with a database reporting about 120 thousand dollars in total, and sold its San Francisco and Oakland operations to the local ISP Monkeybrains in March 2019 on undisclosed terms. The press release describes real customers in Portola and Bayview but no reason for the sale beyond the founders moving to other projects. It reads as a small outcome in a capital heavy field, but the factor chosen is a loose label for an operations sale, not a stated cause.
notes: The seed round rests on a single database (CB Insights, total about 120K); the acquisition press release confirms a seed after YC without an amount. A separate CB Insights page and StartupIntros list 8M seed in December 2023 for a Necto, which is a different company (New York bank API aggregator) and is excluded. Competitor sources are dated August 2018, about five months after the batch, which is noted; the Starry January 2018 launch date comes from a search summary. The website joinnecto.com was live with a 49 dollar plan and 2018 copyright, so status is uncertain. Education and prior employers not found. Exit type is acquisition, which conflicts with the YC inactive flag only mildly.
